title: 1966 AHSME Problem 30
statement: If three of the roots of \(x^4+ax^2+bx+c=0\) are \(1,\) \(2,\) and \(3,\) then the value of \(a+c\) is:

solutions.text:
The fourth root is \(-6\) because the root sum is zero. The sum of pairwise products is \[ \begin{aligned} a&=2+3-6+6\\ &\quad-12-18=-25, \end{aligned} \] while the product is \(c=(1)(2)(3)(-6)=-36.\) Thus \(a+c=-61.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: The missing \(x^3\) coefficient makes the sum of all four roots zero
Use the fourth root to compute the pairwise sum \(a\) and product \(c\)
